observations.what: Loans printed 'S + m % PIK <coupon> %' published pik_rate = m (the margin, which is all the filer tags as PIK) and a positive cash leg, though the whole floating coupon is paid in kind. Population (pik_pop.sql on rftsb): 55 loan rows, 235.9M + 13.2M + Continental 2025-09-30 (printed '7.00 % PIK 11.29 %' without the benchmark); 11 loans: Applitools 2023-03-31 to 2026-06-30, Sweep Purchaser 2024-03-31 on, BP Purchaser 2025-03-31, KWOR other debt 2025-03-31 on, Continental Battery / Acquisition 2025-06-30 on, FPG Intermediate Holdco 2025-09-30 on, Vardiman Black 2025-12-31 on, BPG Holdings IV and Diligent 2026-06-30 (53.1M fair value at 2026-06-30, 12 rows). Evidence: 39 quarter steps of printed par, 28 grow by the coupon not the margin (Applitools 6,827 -> 7,023, +2.87 pct against 11.06/4 = 2.77 and 6.25/4 = 1.56), the rest are non-accrual (flat or below the margin) or delayed-draw moves (pik_growth_sum.sql); Applitools 2023-06-30 prints '11.35 % PIK' in the coupon column. Fixed in rftsc by 54 row corrections (pik_rate = printed coupon, cash leg 0; the 55th row, Applitools 2023-03-31 term loan, already published 11.06 / 0). Evidence strength: the filer's XBRL tags the margin as the PIK rate on these rows (Applitools 0.0625, Diligent 0.0842, BP Purchaser 0.055), so the corrections override the tag by inference; 15 of the 54 corrected rows have no par-growth evidence of their own and rest on the printed format alone (BP Purchaser 2025-03-31, Diligent x2 and BPG 2026-06-30, Continental x5, Vardiman x6; 10 of them on non-accrual; r21.sql), and Continental 2025-09-30 prints no benchmark, read from the same loan's 2025-06-30 and 2025-12-31 lines 'S + 7.00 % PIK 11.29 %'. Convention as Kent (D-218) and Wine.com (Silver Capital): the shared reading is still open on other funds (0001646614 left it as a cohort question). Same round: Applitools 2023-03-31 undrawn revolver, printed '6.25 % 11.06 %' with no PIK word but tagged PIK, PIK withdrawn and interest_rate 11.06 set; Long Term Care Group 2024-03-31 '(incl. 7.00 % PIK)' publishes pik = spread 7.00 with a cash leg 5.57, a different printed form, left.
